items.says: The unrelated Sunrise Bakery entry leads the Experience section and takes as much space as research roles.
items.because: A reader looking for quantitative research sees it before the relevant experience, weakening the first impression.

items.says: The 35% change lacks a named risk-adjusted metric and comparison point.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what changed or assess the result.

items.says: Purged walk-forward splits and an embargo do not by themselves guarantee every decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: They address leakage across split boundaries, not look-ahead elsewhere in the feature and decision pipeline.

items.says: “Validated the signal” gives no finding from the validation.
items.because: The data span and split design show how it was tested, not the result supporting the claim.

items.says: The best of 400 backtest Sharpes is reported as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the maximum can inflate it with noise and does not establish expected live performance.

items.says: The bullet attributes the desk book’s Sharpe increase to the signal without a controlled comparison.
items.because: An out-of-sample backtest after costs does not by itself isolate the signal’s contribution.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker does not establish independent Monte Carlo runs.
items.because: Workers with the same generator and seed can repeat the same random stream.

items.says: The bullet uses the first-person phrase “my proof.”
items.because: It reads like a sentence and draws attention to the writer instead of the result.

items.says: The Holm correction across indices does not establish corrected significance in both crisis periods.
items.because: It controls only the hypotheses included in the correction family.

items.says: “Both crisis periods” does not identify the periods.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which market conditions the result represents.

items.says: “Cut validation leakage” is stronger than the stated fold change establishes.
items.because: Closing the score gap does not show leakage caused it or was reduced.

items.says: The 0.02 gap lacks a score metric and whether it is absolute or relative.
items.because: A reader cannot interpret or compare the discrepancy without that context.
The error can make the skills section look insufficiently checked.

items.says: Kafka is listed without an experience or project example of its use.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the level or context of the skill.
